subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw own a minimal immutable provenance contract in core/SDK and enforce the first review-and-influence policy in builtin memory, or should trust policy remain entirely extension-owned behind existing memory-plugin seams?
rationale: This choice fixes the compatibility boundary for persisted metadata, plugin SDK contracts, migration ownership, and which memory backends must preserve or enforce the policy.

options.title: Core provenance, bounded builtin policy
options.body: Add framework-assigned origin references as a generic contract, then implement only review and influence state for builtin memory while leaving broader scoring, expiry, and UI experiments to plugins.

options.title: Extension-owned trust policy
options.body: Keep core limited to existing memory seams and require an MCP or memory plugin such as the discussed external implementation to own storage and retrieval policy.

recommendation.title: Core provenance, bounded builtin policy
recommendation.body: Add framework-assigned origin references as a generic contract, then implement only review and influence state for builtin memory while leaving broader scoring, expiry, and UI experiments to plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and recent memory-contract history place steipete closest to the necessary core-versus-extension boundary decision.
